title: Revolutionary tribunals and executions at La Cabaña
summary: After the Cuban Revolution's victory, revolutionary tribunals tried officials and police of the Batista government accused of war crimes. Trials at the San Carlos de la Cabaña fortress in Havana began on 19 January 1959, and many defendants were executed by firing squad. Che Guevara commanded the fortress and reviewed appeals; the number of deaths is disputed.

uncertainty.note: Start is the date the fortress trials began per the Brazilian thesis; end is when the tribunals trying alleged war criminals were deactivated (June 1959). Cuba Archive dates Guevara's command at La Cabaña from January 4 to November 26, 1959.

importance.justification: Early revolutionary justice that consolidated the new Cuban government and remains contested over legality and scale.

audience_note: Describes summary trials and firing-squad executions. Casualty figures are contested and are attributed to their sources rather than given as settled.

reviewer_note: Figures by source, not reconciled: the UEL thesis says Fidel Castro acknowledged about 550 executions of accused war criminals (Cuba-wide) and that 207 had already been shot in provinces when the fortress trials began; Cuba Archive (via Werlau) believes about 73 were executed at La Cabaña without basic legal guarantees during Guevara's command, among 123 cases it attributes to him. The sources disagree on legitimacy (UEL describes witness testimony and defence lawyers; Cuba Archive calls them summary trials lasting minutes). Cuba Archive is an advocacy source. Least sure of the counts.
